title: The grapes
subtitle: Cool-climate whites and Pinot
objectives: Describe its Chardonnay and Pinot Noir

steps.title: Sauvignon Blanc
steps.body: Sauvignon Blanc is Casablanca's leading grape, giving crisp wines with citrus, grapefruit, passion fruit, cut grass and a herbal, saline note. The cool climate keeps acidity high and green aromas fresh. It's often compared with New Zealand's style, though usually a little less pungent.

steps.title: Chardonnay and Pinot Noir
steps.body: Chardonnay gives fresh, citrus and stone fruit wines, often with some oak and lees. Pinot Noir gives light, fresh reds with red cherry and strawberry. Syrah, from cooler sites, gives peppery wines. About three-quarters of Casablanca's vineyards are white, which is unusual in red-dominated Chile.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its Casablanca style.

steps.body: Casablanca Sauvignon Blanc is often great value, with fresh, zesty fruit similar to New Zealand's.

steps.prompt: Why do white grapes dominate Casablanca?

steps.title: What you learned
points: Sauvignon Blanc leads, crisp and herbal
Chardonnay and Pinot Noir also thrive
About three-quarters of vineyards are white
